solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Open directory

definitions.meaning: plain to see, obvious, as an adjective
a list, like a ship's cargo list or passenger list

explanation.surface: A command to open up a phone book or a folder on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means obvious or evident, and the noun is a list of cargo or passengers, a kind of listing.

clue.text: Spot test terrified learning establishment leaders

parts.note: the MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test for British cars

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so the first letters of the three words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Pupils at some school are terrified by a surprise test sprung by the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot test' looks like one phrase, but 'Spot' is the definition. 'leaders' takes T, L and E from 'terrified learning establishment'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mottle is to mark with blotches or patches of colour, so spot is a fair verb synonym.

clue.text: French people run into a woman, perhaps

indicators.note: the word run goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a woman is, jokingly, 'no man', not a male
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A French person bumps into a woman somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a woman, perhaps' is a playful definition by example: any woman is not a man. 'run' is the cricket abbreviation, not a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were the people of Normandy in northern France; the singular name serves loosely for that people.

clue.text: Skeleton is standing without radius

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the standing word goes round the letter

parts.note: standing in the sense of renown or reputation, i.e. fame
R is the standard abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: An anatomy model is propped up but missing one forearm bone, the radius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' and the radius a bone, but 'without' here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame is the supporting structure of something, just as a skeleton is the body's supporting structure.

clue.text: Flamboyant display took in the obscure

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, like a guest taken in

parts.note: flamboyant means showy
an ad, short for advertisement, is a public display or notice

explanation.surface: A dazzling show drew in an audience of obscure people.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means dim, vague or hard to make out, which is what obscure means as an adjective.

clue.text: Freezing cold in lorry

indicators.note: the cold letter goes in the lorry word

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck in British usage
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A lorry driver complains it is freezing cold in the cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic is used informally of weather or temperatures that are bitterly cold, like the polar region.

clue.text: Outlaw what mugger might do to conceal himself

parts.note: a mugger robs a victim
a mugger would hide his face by being in a hood

explanation.surface: A tip for an outlawed mugger on how to stay unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Sherwood Forest bandit is the archetypal outlaw of English legend.

clue.text: More than one of these men attempts clothing for a girl

definitions.text: More than one of these men
definitions.note: the definition points to a plural noun naming such men

indicators.note: clothing in the sense of dressing round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: attempts means tries
Ann is a common girl's name

explanation.surface: Men who attempt to dress as a girl, described in the clue's all-in-one picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, cross-dressers trying on women's clothes; the word is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, now offensive slang term for cross-dressers, men in women's clothing, as the clue itself describes.

clue.text: Bless an icon with heads of six elephants mashed together

indicators.note: mashed means crushed into a new shape, so the letters of an icon are rearranged
heads are the first letters of the two words named

explanation.surface: An icon is blessed while half a dozen elephants are squashed together nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bless' is a loose definition: making someone a saint is a formal sanctification rather than a simple blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: To canonise is to declare someone a saint, a formal kind of blessing or sanctifying.

clue.text: Decline to go on holiday

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone away is to refuse or reject them, as a verb phrase meaning decline.

clue.text: Get combat rations handed out alternately

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is given out, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Soldiers collect field rations doled out in turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtain is a slightly formal synonym for get, meaning acquire or come by.

clue.text: Where a busy surgeon might be superior

definitions.text: Where a busy surgeon might be
definitions.meaning: a busy surgeon is at an operation, at an op
placed above or on top of something

explanation.surface: A busy surgeon might be found in a senior role.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on top of, so it fits superior in its literal sense of positioned higher.

clue.text: Misses what trees get in spring

definitions.meaning: trees put out new foliage in spring

explanation.surface: A tree loses out on its spring foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means omits or fails to include, and literally describes foliage coming out on trees.

clue.text: What some knights say to no French fabric

parts.note: the Knights Who Say Ni appear in the comedy film Monty Python and the Holy Grail
non is French for no

explanation.surface: Knights refusing a cloth in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The knights are from Monty Python and the Holy Grail, who demand a shrubbery and shout 'Ni!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer dress fabric, a type of chiffon-like material.

clue.text: Mole was wanting in the capacity of male chromosome

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for in the role or capacity of
the Y chromosome is carried only by males

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal lacking the capacity of a male chromosome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is not the animal but a stone pier or breakwater; 'was wanting' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone pier or breakwater at a harbour, which serves as a wharf for boats.

clue.text: In this country, Iranian is disguised as East European

parts.note: for a British setter, this country is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: a disguised word has its letters rearranged to hide it

explanation.surface: An Iranian living in Britain passes himself off as an Eastern European.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is in Eastern Europe, so its citizens are East Europeans.

clue.text: Bravery that hurts newspapers on both sides

indicators.note: the newspapers word sits either side of the cry of pain

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
ow is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A brave story that pains the newspapers on either side of politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is skill or daring in combat, so it overlaps with bravery or valour.

clue.text: After taking off top, repair strapless dresses

indicators.note: to repair is to fix or make anew, so the letters are rebuilt
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, removed here

explanation.surface: Someone mending a strapless dress after removing the top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' looks like the garments but is a verb, as in dressing wounds. 'taking off top' drops the first S, leaving TRAPLESS for 'repair' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To plaster a wound is to cover it with a sticking plaster, which is a way of dressing it.

clue.text: Smart salesman gets exhausted

parts.note: to smart is to sting or burn with pain
a tout pushes sales, often of tickets

explanation.surface: A sharp-suited salesman ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone burnt-out is worn out from overwork, a common idiom for exhausted.

clue.text: "Blinds with science" is initially written by home of art

indicators.note: written next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: the Louvre in Paris is a world-famous art museum

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: 'Blinds with science' is a phrase scrawled at a famous museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blinds with science' is a set phrase meaning baffle with jargon, but 'Blinds' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Louvres are slatted window shutters, a kind of window blind.

clue.text: Philosopher didn't finish chronicle on irrational number

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a saga is a long chronicle or narrative
e, the base of natural logarithms, is an irrational number

explanation.surface: A thinker abandoned his history of an irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise person, the kind of thinker one might call a philosopher.

clue.text: Headed West to steal diamonds

indicators.note: to steal is to take in, so the jewels are pocketed inside the name

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood film star
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Someone travelled west to rob a jewel store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made for a place is to have headed towards it, a sense of travel direction.

clue.text: Hot molten rocks used as decongestant

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Volcanic lava is used as a cold remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun for the lava, but it is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Menthol, from mint oil, is used in inhalants and lozenges to relieve nasal congestion.

clue.text: Firstly, air pumped in to puncture spare tyre

indicators.note: air pumped into a tyre goes inside, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to punch a hole is to puncture something

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Air is pumped in to repair a punctured spare wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare tyre' is not a wheel but a roll of fat round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is slang for a roll of belly fat, which is what a paunch is.

clue.text: Society destroys facilities

parts.note: kills means destroys or wrecks

explanation.surface: A society wrecks the amenities provided.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility for something is an aptitude or talent, so facilities are abilities.

clue.text: Break the Ten Commandments on road to where they were received

parts.note: to break God's laws is to sin
the A1 is the Great North Road in Britain, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Breaking the Ten Commandments on the way to where Moses received them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible places the giving of the Ten Commandments to Moses on Mount Sinai.

clue.text: Chasing king, mob work out how to get on board ship

definitions.text: how to get on board ship

indicators.note: the king comes after, chasing the other pieces

parts.note: a mob or gang of people
to plan is to work out a scheme
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gang pursuing a king plots how to get aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable walkway used to board or leave a ship.

clue.text: Inspire 18th alternative to Plan B?

parts.note: taken as written from Plan B
counting eighteen letters on from B in the alphabet lands on T, an alternative to B

explanation.surface: A fallback plan offered as the eighteenth option.
explanation.walkthrough: Plan B is a fallback; moving B eighteen places along the alphabet gives T, so 'Plan T' is the eighteenth alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant an idea in someone's mind is loosely to inspire or instil it, a loose equivalence.

clue.text: Striking old girlfriend about the ears

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
otic means relating to the ears

explanation.surface: A former girlfriend hits someone round the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like hitting, but it is the adjective meaning eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means strikingly unusual or colourful, a near synonym of striking as an adjective.

clue.text: Fragments of shell almost strike knight in the heart

indicators.note: the other pieces go into the middle of the shortened word
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is struck in the heart by shell fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fragments of shell' looks like the whole definition, but 'shell almost' gives SHEL, which takes RAP and N in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is the metal splinters thrown out by an exploding shell or bomb.

clue.text: Protest against good location

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupying a building

explanation.surface: A protest against a good spot being chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting is the placing of something, i.e. its position or location.

clue.text: Grasps desire I lacked to crack signs

indicators.note: cracking something opens it so another piece can go in

parts.note: clues are signs or indications

indicators.note: the named letter is missing from the word

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Someone who lacked any wish to decipher signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I lacked' reads like a confession, but it tells you to drop the letter I from the desire word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutches as a verb means seizes or grips tightly, much the same as grasps.
